categories.name: AI & ML Security
categories.summary: Critical research from the Cloud Security Alliance highlights prompt injection vulnerabilities in agentic CI/CD workflows, specifically targeting GitHub Actions with Claude Code integration. This represents an emerging attack vector where trust boundary failures allow external actors to inject malicious instructions into AI agent workflows, expanding the traditional supply chain threat model.

key_items.title: Claude Code GitHub Action Vulnerable to Prompt Injection
key_items.detail: CSA research note documents how CI/CD pipelines treating untrusted GitHub App actors as trusted create prompt injection attack surfaces, requiring permission checks and actor validation as defensive measures.

top_insights: Prompt injection is evolving beyond direct LLM attacks into CI/CD supply chain compromises, with agentic workflows creating new trust boundary vulnerabilities that traditional security models don't address.
The security community continues integrating AI capabilities into defensive tooling, with established platforms like REMnux adding AI-assisted analysis features.
Conference content aggregation indicates sustained community investment in knowledge sharing across offensive security, vulnerability management, and SOC operations domains.
Fractional security leadership services remain a growing market segment as organizations balance security governance needs against budget constraints.
